# Temple Scroll Column 56 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 56 where the three translators significantly diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 56:2 — levirate marriage terminology

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "perform-the-duty-of-a-brother-in-law" | Literal yibbem — compound preserving the technical Hebrew term |
| LOGOS | "perform the duty of a brother-in-law" | Same content, standard English formatting |
| PNEUMA | "fulfill his obligation as her husband's brother" | Modern paraphrase of the levirate duty |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering. The technical levirate term should be preserved, but without EMET's hyphenated compound.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 56:7 — "One-Whose-Sandal-Was-Pulled-Off" vs. "Unsandaled"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "The House of the One-Whose-Sandal-Was-Pulled-Off" | Literal chaluts ha-na'al — full descriptive compound |
| LOGOS | "the House of the Unsandaled" | Concise rendering preserving the social stigma |
| PNEUMA | "the family of the man whose sandal was pulled off" | Explanatory rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "the House of the Unsandaled" (LOGOS). Concise and memorable; EMET's compound is unwieldy and PNEUMA loses the formulaic quality.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 56:8 — "shameful-parts" vs. "private parts" vs. "genitals"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "shameful-parts" | Literal mevushav — from the root b-w-sh "to be ashamed" |
| LOGOS | "private parts" | Euphemistic English equivalent maintaining decorum |
| PNEUMA | "genitals" | Direct anatomical term |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "private parts" (LOGOS). Maintains appropriate register for legal/sacred text while being clear. "Shameful-parts" imports a judgment not in the original; "genitals" is too clinical.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 56:10-11 — "stone and stone" vs. "two different weights"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a stone and a stone, a great and a small" | Literal Hebrew idiom for dishonest weights |
| LOGOS | "two different weights, one heavy and one light" | Standard English interpretation of the Hebrew idiom |
| PNEUMA | "two sets of weights — one heavy, one light" | Modern commercial language |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering. The Hebrew idiom "stone and stone" is opaque in English; LOGOS clarifies while preserving the legal specificity.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 56:16 — "multiply horses" vs. "acquire many horses" vs. "build up a large stable"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "multiply to himself horses" | Literal yarbeh — the standard Deuteronomic prohibition verb |
| LOGOS | "acquire many horses" | Clear English equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "build up a large stable of horses" | Vivid rendering making the military concern visible |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "acquire many horses" (LOGOS). "Multiply" is too literal in modern English; PNEUMA's "stable" adds imagery not in the text.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 56:19 — "fear" vs. "revere"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "fear the LORD his God" | Literal yir'ah — the standard Hebrew term |
| LOGOS | "fear the LORD his God" | Same — traditional rendering preserved |
| PNEUMA | "revere the LORD his God" | "Revere" conveys respectful awe rather than terror |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "fear" (EMET/LOGOS). This is the standard rendering of yir'at YHWH throughout the biblical corpus and should be maintained for consistency.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---
